title: Podgora, Croatia: First-Time Visitor Guide 2027
metaDescription: Podgora first-timer guide for 2027: beaches, getting there from Split, where to stay, costs in euros, Biokovo, island ferries and practical local tips.
content:
## Where Is Podgora and How Do You Get There?

Podgora sits on the Makarska Riviera in central Dalmatia. It lies between Tučepi to the north-west and Drašnice and Igrane to the south. Split is about 70 km away and Makarska about 9–10 km. The town has roughly 1,200–1,500 residents, so it stays small even in August.

### From Split Airport
- **Rental car:** The drive takes about 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes via the A1 motorway and the coastal road. A car gives the most freedom for Biokovo and the islands.
- **Bus:** Regional buses run from Split along the coast. Allow 1.5–2 hours with stops. Expect about €8–12 depending on the operator and season.
- **Private transfer:** Usually €60–90 per vehicle. This is worthwhile for groups of three or more.

### Getting to the Islands
The nearest ferries are at Makarska for Brač (Sumartin) and at Drvenik for Hvar (Sućuraj). Check the Jadrolinija timetable in July and August and arrive early with a vehicle.

## Best Time to Visit Podgora

The swimming season runs from May to October. July and August are the hottest and busiest months, with sea temperatures of about 24–26 °C. June and September are the best balance: warm sea, lower prices and easier parking. Many restaurants close or cut hours from late October.

## Podgora Beaches: What to Expect

All beaches here are pebble or gravel. Bring water shoes. Entry is free, and loungers and umbrellas are rented at the busier spots.

- **Town beach (centre):** The most convenient. It has changing facilities, rental loungers and umbrellas, and cafés directly behind it. It also has an access ramp and a sea lift for disabled swimmers.
- **Plišivac:** North of the port. Palm trees give some natural shade, and cafés are close by. Sections are narrow, so arrive before 10:00 in peak season.
- **Garma:** Further north, smaller and rockier. It suits visitors who want fewer people.
- **Drvenik side and Čaklje:** The southern end of the promenade has quieter stretches.
- **Dračevac:** Between Tučepi and Podgora, and a good option on calm days.

A set of two loungers and an umbrella usually costs about €15–30 per day in July and August. The cheaper alternative is a towel on the free sections, which is what most locals do.

## Things to Do in Podgora

### Walk the Promenade
A seafront promenade links the beaches, the harbour and the restaurants. A full walk from one end of town to the other takes about 30–40 minutes. The route continues toward Tučepi, so a long evening stroll is easy.

### See the Seagull Wings Monument
The monument above the town is the most recognisable landmark in Podgora. It is a free stop and gives a good view over the coast. Upper Podgora, the older part of the town, is on a slope, so wear proper shoes.

### Hike or Drive Up Biokovo
Biokovo Nature Park rises directly behind the town. The Skywalk, a glass viewing platform near the summit, can be reached by guided quad tours from Makarska or by car on a steep road. Go early in the morning. Temperatures at the top can be 10 °C or more cooler than on the coast, so take a jacket.

### Kayak and SUP
Kayak and stand-up paddleboard rentals operate along the beaches in season. Prices are typically €10–15 per hour. Mornings usually have the calmest water.

## Day Trips From Podgora

| Destination | Distance | Why go |
|---|---|---|
| Makarska | 9–10 km | Old town, Riva promenade, restaurants, bars |
| Tučepi | Next to Podgora | Long pebble beach of about 4 km |
| Brela (Punta Rata) | About 20 km | Blue Flag beach and the pine-topped Brela Stone |
| Hvar via Drvenik–Sućuraj | About 30 km to port | Island beaches and Hvar Town |
| Brač via Makarska–Sumartin | About 10 km to port | Quieter island landscape |
| Krka Waterfalls | About 2 hours by road | Waterfalls and walkways |

Punta Rata is the headline beach of the region, but it is crowded in summer. Go before 09:00 or after 17:00.

A Makarska speedboat tour covering Brač, Hvar and a blue lagoon stop is the easiest way to see islands without a car. Book a morning departure.

## Where to Stay in Podgora

Podgora is known for private apartments and small guesthouses rather than large resorts. A few hotels sit along the coast between Podgora and Tučepi.

- **Apartments:** About €60–120 per night in peak season for two people, and about €40–70 in June and September.
- **Hotels:** Typically €100–220 per night for a double in July and August.
- **Location tip:** Choose accommodation within 300 m of the promenade. Upper Podgora has views but involves steep climbs back from the beach.

Podgora is the better base for peace, families and walkers. Makarska is better for nightlife, with bars and a livelier evening scene. Staying in Podgora and taking the bus to Makarska is the sensible compromise.

## Food and Drink

Local cooking centres on Dalmatian seafood: grilled fish, black risotto, octopus salad and *peka* (slow-cooked meat or octopus under an iron bell, usually ordered in advance). Typical prices are:

- Coffee: €1.50–2.50
- Pizza or pasta: €9–15
- Grilled fish: about €50–80 per kilogram, sold by weight
- Main course in a harbour restaurant: €15–28

Fish is priced by weight, so ask the weight and total before ordering. Restaurants on the harbour front charge more than the streets one block inland. Local supermarkets are the cheapest option for lunch and picnic supplies.

## Getting Around

The town centre is walkable. Buses on the coastal road connect Podgora with Makarska, Tučepi, Split and Dubrovnik. Parking in July and August is the biggest daily frustration. Many apartments include a private space, so confirm this before booking. A rental car is not necessary for a beach stay, but it is the better tool for Biokovo, small coves and island ferries.

## Local Tips for First-Time Visitors

1. **Take water shoes.** Pebbles are hot by midday and sea urchins live on rocky sections.
2. **Swim early or late.** Beaches are quietest before 10:00 and after 17:00.
3. **Carry some cash.** Most places take cards, but small cafés, beach rentals and market stalls often prefer cash.
4. **Skip organised day trips to Dubrovnik.** The drive is about 2.5 hours each way, which leaves very little time in the city. It is better to stay two nights there or keep to the islands and Biokovo.
5. **Book summer ferries ahead for vehicles.** Queues at Drvenik are long on weekends.
6. **Pack a sun layer.** Dalmatian summer sun is strong, and shade is limited on several beaches.
7. **The Skywalk is only worth it in clear weather.** On cloudy days the view is poor and the price is wasted.

The marketing for the busiest Makarska Riviera boat tours makes them sound more remote than they are. In July and August, popular stops are crowded, so a smaller or earlier tour is better value.

## Is Podgora Worth Visiting?

Podgora suits visitors who want a quiet harbour town, accessible beaches and an easy base for the region. It is less suited to travellers who want large clubs, big shopping streets or a historic old town. Those are in Makarska, a short bus ride away.

faq.question: Is Podgora good for first-time visitors to Croatia?
faq.answer: Yes. It is small, walkable and calm, with pebble beaches, a promenade and easy access to Makarska, Biokovo and island ferries. It is best for relaxed beach holidays rather than nightlife.

faq.question: How far is Podgora from Split Airport?
faq.answer: Podgora is about 70 km from Split Airport. By car or private transfer the trip takes roughly 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes. Regional buses take about 1.5–2 hours.

faq.question: What is the best time to visit Podgora?
faq.answer: June and September are the best months, with warm sea, fewer crowds and lower prices. July and August are hottest and busiest. The swimming season runs from May to October.

faq.question: Are Podgora beaches sandy?
faq.answer: No. The beaches are pebble or gravel, with some rocky sections. Water shoes are recommended for comfort and to protect against sea urchins.

faq.question: Is Podgora better than Makarska as a base?
faq.answer: Podgora is quieter and better for families and rest. Makarska has the old town, bars and more restaurants. Many visitors stay in Podgora and take the 9–10 km bus ride to Makarska for evenings.

faq.question: Do I need a car in Podgora?
faq.answer: Not for a beach stay, as the centre is walkable and buses serve the coast. A car is helpful for Biokovo, remote coves and the Drvenik ferry. Check for parking at your accommodation in summer.

faq.question: How much does a day in Podgora cost?
faq.answer: A moderate daily budget in peak season is about €60–100 per person excluding accommodation. That covers coffee, a restaurant meal, beach rentals and a bus trip. Prices drop in June and September.

quickAnswer: Podgora is a calm harbour town on the Makarska Riviera, about 70 km from Split and 9–10 km from Makarska. First-time visitors should plan on pebble beaches, a seafront promenade, day trips to Makarska, Biokovo and the islands, and a visit between May and October. A car is useful but not essential.
